correctness.rationale: One triangle has probability 1/4 of being cyclic even conditional on the direction of any one of its edges. Distinct triangles share at most one edge, so all pairs are independent. Among three triangles, if one shares at most one edge with the union of the other two, it is independent of their pair by the same conditioning, giving the full joint law. Otherwise each pair shares a different edge. Starting with abc and abd, the third must contain ac and ad or bc and bd, hence is acd or bcd. The three shared edges are spokes at one vertex. Simultaneous cyclicity would require each pair of spokes to have opposite directions at that vertex, which is impossible. This gives centered mixed moment -1/64 in the exceptional case by pair independence. The all-equal term is 3/32, the two-equal terms vanish, and each exceptional unordered triple contributes six times -1/64. There are exactly four such triples per K4 and they determine the clique uniquely. Mean, variance and inversion for the clique count follow with the stated coefficients. Empty and short families and arbitrary fixed signed weights are covered; no assumption of biased or dependent edge sampling is used. The accompanying finite checker was inspected, not executed.
